technical_and_design_decisions: Base all development on Spring Boot 3.x to align with Spring Framework 6.0+ Java 17+ requirements and leverage existing Spring ecosystem tooling.
For Azure Event Hubs integration (U1), use the official Spring Cloud Azure Event Hubs starter library to minimize custom implementation and ensure compatibility with Azure services.
For IPython Notebook integration (U2), leverage the existing Spring XD shell extension framework to add Jupyter kernel support, reusing existing command execution logic.
For upgrade config preservation (U3), implement a version-aware migration utility that runs during Spring XD upgrade, with checksum validation to ensure config files are not corrupted during copy.

For direct module binding (U4), extend the Spring Cloud Stream binder SPI to add a 'direct' binder type that uses in-process Spring Integration channels instead of external middleware, with configurable latency optimization flags.
For xd-admin REST APIs (U5), use Spring Web MVC with Spring HATEOAS for API design, and integrate with existing Spring XD role-based access control (RBAC) for security.
For ModuleRegistry stubs (U6), use Mockito to create mock implementations of the ModuleRegistry interface, with pre-configured test module definitions that match common stream pipeline use cases.
For repo migration (U7), perform a modular refactor of the spring-cloud-stream-modules codebase to remove s-c-s specific dependencies, and add OpenAPI 3.0 documentation for all public module APIs.

For in-memory stream definition repo (U8), implement the StreamDefinitionRepository interface using a thread-safe ConcurrentHashMap, with no persistence layer, and add a dev profile activation flag to enable it only in non-production environments.

The s-c-s and s-c repositories referenced in U4 and U7 are accessible Spring Cloud repositories with write permissions for the development team, and have established contribution guidelines.

The in-memory stream definition repository specified in U8 is intended for development and testing use only, so no requirements for data persistence, backup, recovery, or multi-instance consistency are needed.
All user stories are independent and can be developed in parallel without conflicting changes to shared core framework components.
